documents.abstract: Reliable preoperative classification and outcome prediction could improve management of locally advanced colorectal cancer. We retrospectively studied 879 participants from two centers, including 741 patients with locally advanced colorectal cancer and 138 with benign colorectal lesions. Clinical, radiomics, deep learning, and early fusion models were trained at center A ( n = 615) and independently tested at center B ( n = 264) using pretreatment contrast-enhanced computed tomography and clinical data. The clinical-radiomics nomogram achieved a test AUC of 0.957 for benign-malignant classification. For 3-year and 5-year overall survival, radiomics achieved test AUCs of 0.874 and 0.898, while fusion achieved 0.870 and 0.899, respectively. These findings identify CT radiomics as a promising digital biomarker for colorectal cancer stratification and show that early deep learning fusion offers limited incremental value over an optimized radiomics baseline.

documents.abstract: Background The increasing integration of technology in education has transformed English language teaching, giving rise to multimodal learning strategies that combine text, visuals, audio, and interactive tools. While these approaches are widely adopted, there remains limited synthesized evidence on how they specifically influence students’ English-speaking skills across educational levels. This study addresses this gap by examining the effectiveness of multimodal strategies in developing speaking proficiency. Methods Using a systematic literature review (SLR) design guided by PRISMA protocols, relevant studies published between 2020 and 2026 were retrieved from ProQuest and ScienceDirect databases. From an initial pool of 2,499 articles, eight studies met the inclusion criteria. These studies included participants from elementary, secondary, and tertiary levels and explored approaches such as translanguaging, augmented reality (AR), artificial intelligence (AI), extended reality (XR), and other multimodal strategies. Results Findings reveal that multimodal strategies generally improve students’ speaking skills, particularly in terms of fluency, vocabulary, pronunciation, and confidence. Conclusion Translanguaging enhances participation and meaning-making, while AI-enhanced tools provide interactive and low-anxiety environments for speaking practice. However, some approaches show uneven effects, particularly in developing grammatical accuracy, and may be less effective when overused.

Literature reviews on the ethics of artificial intelligence (AI) in human resource management (HRM) have multiplied quickly, and the result is an evidence base that is abundant but scattered. Practitioners seeking guidance grounded in evidence have nowhere consolidated to turn. This study addresses that problem through an umbrella review, conducted under Joanna Briggs Institute guidance and reported according to the PRISMA 2020 statement. A structured Scopus search produced a final corpus of thirteen peer-reviewed systematic and scoping reviews, published between 2020 and 2026. We analysed the corpus in two stages: a quantitative, descriptive mapping, then a six-phase qualitative thematic analysis. The mapping shows a field that consolidated only very recently; ten of the thirteen reviews appeared in 2025, and recruitment and selection dominate the contexts studied. Fairness is the concern the reviews examine most fully. Well-being is the one they examine least. The thematic analysis organised the evidence into three macro-themes, trust dynamics in AI-enabled HRM, algorithmic fairness and bias mitigation, and employee well-being and vulnerability, and showed that the literature has treated these as isolated questions. Our main contribution is the Integrated Ethical AI-HRM Framework, which orders the three pillars into a single structure: fairness and transparency condition employee trust, trust in turn shapes well-being, and the long-term durability of workplace AI depends on mitigating algorithmic bias and keeping algorithmic reasoning explainable.

documents.abstract: The exponential expansion of the global wind power industry has precipitated a novel environmental and occupational health challenge: exposure to complex acoustic environments characterized by low-frequency sound (LFS) and infrasound. This specific mixed sound field, prevalent in and around wind farms, is intricately linked to the controversial “Wind Turbine Syndrome”(WTS). Despite growing epidemiological complaints, the systematic health impacts and the underlying neurobiological mechanisms of this composite acoustic environment remain insufficiently elucidated. This review aims to synthesize the acoustic characteristics, epidemiological evidence, psychological impacts, central nervous system (CNS) mechanisms, and behavioral alterations induced by LFS and infrasound exposure. We conducted a comprehensive synthesis of data derived from field acoustic measurements in wind farms, epidemiological surveys of occupational and community populations, and experimental animal models. The literature review encompasses biophysical resonance models, molecular neurobiology, and behavioral phenotyping. Infrasound and LFS possess unique physical properties, including prolonged wavelengths and structural penetration, facilitating tissue biomechanical resonance. Exposure to this composite sound field induces a spectrum of symptoms, notably sleep disturbances, cognitive deficits, and emotional dysregulation (anxiety, depression). Based on animal models, the underlying CNS mechanisms are multifaceted, involving mechanotransduction-mediated ion homeostasis disruption (e.g., Ca 2+ ), neurotransmitter system imbalances (5-HT, Glu, GABA, ACh), neuroinflammation driven by glial activation, synaptic structural damage. These mechanisms remain hypothetical in the context of human environmental exposure, pending direct clinical validation. Notably, a bidirectional “dose-effect window” may exists, where low-level infrasound may activate antioxidant pathways to exert neuroprotective effects, high-level exposure may trigger neurodegenerative changes. Animal behavioral models provide supporting evidence consistent with these neurobiological shifts, demonstrating suppressed exploratory behaviors and enhanced anxiety/depression-like phenotypes. LFS and infrasound pose complex risks to the integrity of the CNS in preclinical models. Although the current evidence is not sufficient to immediately mandate a comprehensive revision of occupational exposure limits, the reasonable assumptions generated by animal models emphasize the need for more research on these mechanisms in future studies. In the interim, public health monitoring and urban planning strategies should adopt a precautionary approach, exploring the integration of low-frequency and infrasound-specific evaluations alongside traditional metrics to better characterize the acoustic environment in the future.

documents.abstract: This article examines how algorithmic management and neurotechnologies transform occupational risks and the employer’s duty of prevention. Drawing on a legal review of publications from 2015 to 2025 and a doctrinal, functional, and comparative analysis, it examines psychosocial, cognitive, discriminatory, and other risks associated with the processing of neural data. The study compares the safeguards established under European law, International Labour Organization standards, and the Peruvian legal framework governing occupational safety and health, data protection, and artificial intelligence. It identifies difficulties in assessing risks arising from opaque systems, supervising automated decision-making, and safeguarding workers’ right to defend themselves against disciplinary measures. The article proposes clarifying preventive obligations through the provision of clear and comprehensible information, meaningful human involvement in decisions producing significant effects, participatory risk assessments, and limits on the processing of mental data. In the Peruvian context, it distinguishes existing legal obligations from proposed regulatory measures.

Art is devalued once it is attributed to artificial intelligence (AI). Whether this anti-AI bias is a generic penalty for non-original works or specific to the absence of a human author is unknown, as is how long it lasts. In a preregistered study, 324 participants rated 48 genuine human paintings, each presented as an Original, a human Forgery or AI-Generated, on beauty, valence, meaningfulness and monetary worth, then judged how synthetic (AI vs. human) and authentic (copy vs. original) each was. Forgeries were rated below Originals on every dimension, and AI-Generated works about twice as low, the AI-specific penalty falling most heavily on meaningfulness. The labels did not alter gaze, and their effects did not depend on the emotional content or personal relevance of the artworks. Artworks labelled AI-Generated were judged more synthetic and, less clearly, Forgeries less original, and the more beautiful an artwork, the more likely it was judged human-made, even when unlabelled. About six weeks later (n = 220), after learning that all artworks were human originals, participants no longer rated previously AI-labelled works as less beautiful. They had forgotten the labels but remembered what they had believed, and reconstructed the labels from these beliefs and their initial appraisal. The bias tracked attitudes toward AI, not interoceptive sensibility or visual imagery. The anti-AI bias thus combines a generic non-originality penalty with a penalty specific to the missing human author: it acts at the moment of judgment, yet leaves beliefs that outlast the memory of the label.

documents.abstract: Background Occupational stress affects not only healthcare-worker wellbeing but also organisational stability and patient safety. Evidence linking occupational stress to these downstream outcomes is scarce for Sierra Leone. This study examined the association between occupational stress and burnout, turnover intention, absenteeism and patient-safety outcomes among healthcare workers at Bo Government Hospital. Methods A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 260 healthcare workers selected by stratified proportionate random sampling. Occupational stress was measured with the 10-item Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) and treated as the exposure. Outcomes were burnout dimensions (emotional exhaustion, depersonalisation, reduced personal accomplishment), self-reported turnover intention, absenteeism exceeding three days per month, and patient-safety events (medication errors and near-miss incidents in the preceding three months). Associations were assessed using Pearson's chi-square tests in SPSS v26, with significance set at p < 0.05. Results Among workers with high occupational stress, emotional exhaustion was present in 61.2%, reduced personal accomplishment in 53.8% and depersonalisation in 44.7%. Turnover intention was substantially higher among highly stressed workers than among those with low or moderate stress (56.4% vs 22.1%; χ² = 38.4, df = 1, p < 0.001), as was absenteeism exceeding three days per month (38.2% vs 14.6%). Patient-safety outcomes were also elevated: 22.7% of highly stressed workers reported a medication error and 31.5% a near-miss incident in the preceding three months, compared with 8.9% and 12.3% respectively among less-stressed workers. Conclusions High occupational stress is strongly associated with burnout, intention to leave and patient-safety events among healthcare workers at Bo Government Hospital. Occupational stress is therefore both a workforce-wellbeing and a patient-safety concern, and institutional psychosocial support, retention strategies and safety-culture interventions are warranted. However, a systematic evaluation approach of the remanufacturing system design is essential before deploying new HRC workstations. This paper presents a decision-making method, leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), to streamline the quantification of process quality metrics. By processing scenario descriptions, the LLM autonomously assigns metric values, enabling efficient, data-driven assessment of workstation configurations. The deployed system’s architecture, data pipeline, and prompt engineering strategy are also detailed. A case study from the household appliance sector is used to validate the approach leading to enhanced robustness, adaptability, and efficiency while also reducing manual engineering effort while supporting optimal workstation design.

documents.abstract: Hallucination research in low-resource languages fragments easily: each newly named failure mode prompts its own dataset, spending scarce annotators on incomparable resources. We argue for consolidation and test it at community scale. Alikbachan is a Bengali hallucination-detection benchmark stratified along three crossed axes: a human-validated cultural-distance band, six task types, and a five-family, 32-mode hallucination taxonomy. It comprises a harvested 2,516-item test set (Phase 1) and a quota-constructed, gold-labeled 5,000-item set (Phase 2). The stratification is diagnostic. Four zero-shot LLM judges vary by over 30 macro-F1 points across strata, and the item-level predictions of 99 Phase-1 and 32 Phase-2 competition systems reproduce the profile: discourse-level omission defeats judges and most teams alike, whereas only a minority over-flag negative controls. The judges' verdict probabilities rank items well (ROC-AUC 0.74-0.95) but are overconfident (ECE 0.04-0.29). An open competition on Alikbachan drew 222 teams and 3,566 submissions, and a single-prompt 32B judge reaches the 57th percentile. Of the 25 teams in both phases, 24 regress on Phase 2 (mean $-17.6$ points) while every zero-shot judge improves, and Phase-1 rank barely predicts Phase-2 rank (Spearman $ρ=0.35$), so a Phase-1 leaderboard alone would have crowned a different winner.

Modern computer operating systems require users to navigate multiple menus, folders, and applications to complete everyday tasks. This process can be time-consuming and challenging, especially for users with limited technical knowledge. This research paper presents OpenDesk AI, an intelligent desktop assistant designed to simplify computer interactions using Natural Language Processing (NLP). The system allows users to perform tasks such as searching for files, monitoring CPU and memory usage, managing applications, and automating routine desktop activities through natural language commands. OpenDesk AI follows a local-first architecture, where user data and system operations are processed locally to improve privacy, security, and response speed. The proposed system uses intent recognition and entity extraction to understand user commands and execute the corresponding operations through operating system interfaces. It combines natural language understanding with system monitoring and task automation to provide a more accessible and efficient computing experience. The experimental results reported in this study show an intent classification accuracy of 94.6% and task execution time reductions ranging from 84% to 89.12% compared with traditional manual operations. These findings suggest that OpenDesk AI can improve user productivity, reduce repetitive manual work, and provide a practical approach to privacy-focused desktop automation. Keywords: Desktop Automation, Artificial Intelligence, Natural Language Processing, Intent Recognition, Semantic File Search, System Monitoring, Local-First Architecture, Human-Computer Interaction.

Organic framework nanozymes, encompassing metal–organic, covalent–organic, and emerging hydrogen–bonded organic frameworks, are investigated as catalytic materials for portable sensing. Their tunable metal nodes, organic ligands, pore structures, defect sites, and supramolecular microenvironments enable the construction of peroxidase-, oxidase-, catalase-, hydrolase-, and laccase-mimetic activities. Meanwhile, smartphones can assist these systems by providing image acquisition, illumination, RGB/HSV color analysis, fluorescence recording, chemiluminescence capture, data processing and portable quantitative readout, allowing conventional laboratory assays to be transformed into on-site sensing platforms. This review summarizes recent progress from 2022 to 2026 in smartphone-assisted organic framework nanozyme sensing platforms, with emphasis on catalytic signal generation, framework design, smartphone-assisted image processing, and applications in biomedical analysis, food safety, and environmental monitoring. Furthermore, the review delves into the main challenges and future directions, including in-depth analysis of catalytic mechanisms, enhancement of selectivity, standardization of imaging techniques, signal modulation assisted by artificial intelligence, device integration, and performance validation in real samples. This review aims to provide practical guidance for the development of organic framework nanozyme sensing platforms that combine catalytic signal amplification, portability, and smartphone-assisted optical analysis, thereby promoting their application in real-time detection and on-site analysis.

The Proceedings of the ACM on Networking (PACMNET) series showcases top-tier research in emerging computer networks and their applications. We welcome submissions introducing new technologies, innovative experiments, creative applications of networking technologies, and fresh insights gained through analysis. Supported by the ACM Special Interest Group on Communications and Computer Networks (SIGCOMM), the journal is backed by a distinguished Editorial Board composed of leading researchers in the field. This issue constitutes the fourth issue of the fourth volume of PACMNET and features articles submitted to the June 2026 deadline that were accepted. This issue marks the completion of PACMNET's fourth year and reflects the journal's steady growth and increasing maturity. Since its launch in 2023, the number of published research articles has grown from 24 in its first year to 32 in 2024, 50 in 2025, and 60 in 2026. A total of 172 submissions were received for this cycle and underwent a rigorous review process involving 95 Editors, coordinated by two Associate Editors. During the initial phase, each submission received a minimum of three reviews. Submissions that progressed to the second phase were evaluated through at least two additional reviews per article. Following a second round of reviews, the Editors convened online to determine which submissions should be accepted with minor revisions subject to shepherding, which should be invited for a one-shot major revision, and which should be rejected. At the conclusion of this process, 25 articles were accepted, with the authors asked to implement minor revisions under the guidance of a shepherd and included in this issue of PACMNET. The articles in this issue span programmable data planes, Internet infrastructure and transport protocols, and network measurement. Contributions on in-network intelligence include model reconfiguration, adaptive packet classification, and collective communication, alongside transport research on congestion control for distributed training, TCP pacing, and microburst elimination. Measurement studies cover DNS interception, NTP infrastructure, 5G handover inefficiencies, cellular interference, shared IP addresses, and P2P monitoring, while satellite networking contributions examine LEO routing and the suitability of Starlink for live video. Additional work addresses censorship evasion, DoS defense, eBPF diagnostics, BGP traffic engineering, and optical control planes. Collectively, these papers reflect the growing convergence of machine learning, systems design, and large-scale measurement in modern networking research. As usual, we would like to express our sincere gratitude to all those who contributed to this issue of PACMNET, especially the Authors for submitting their finest work and the Associate Editors for offering valuable feedback in their reviews and engaging in the discussions. Our thanks also go to the SIGCOMM Executive Committee Chair and the CoNEXT Steering Committee members for their continued support and guidance, providing essential suggestions and insights throughout the article selection process.

Large language models demonstrate strong medical question-answering capabilities, yet reasoning performance remains uneven across languages. Process reward models (PRMs) provide step-level feedback for improving reasoning, but a fixed PRM may become increasingly misaligned with the trajectory distribution of an evolving policy during reinforcement learning, thereby reducing the reliability of its supervision. We propose a policy--reward alternating training framework that jointly adapts a medical PRM and optimizes a multilingual reasoning policy. Following supervised initialization, the current policy generates multilingual trajectories to update the PRM, which then provides process-level rewards for the next policy update. Medical step supervision maintains the PRM's medical foundation, while process, outcome, and language-related rewards guide policy learning. We develop multilingual medical PRMs (PAIR-PRM) and reasoning models (PAIR-MED) at 8B and 9B scales across 12 languages. On the medical subsets of Global-MMLU and MMLU-ProX, our models improve average accuracy by 3.01--7.47% over their corresponding Qwen backbones. On CUREMED-BENCH, PAIR-MED-9B improves the joint language consistency and logical accuracy metric by 12.88% and 7.45% over baselines for in-domain and out-of-domain languages. Further analyses examine PRM adaptation, multilingual reasoning quality, and the contributions of individual training components.

Present artificial intelligence agents are constructed by means of a coupling between a fixed language model with a general computing device. We show that this coupling makes safety undecidable. In particular, we show that given some dangerous program, no algorithm can predict whether an agent will run such a program that is semantically equivalent. In general, guardrails, blacklists, whitelists and certifications can only lead to imperfect safety solutions. Under finite constraints (bounded context, values and running time) safety is decidable but still intractable. Specifically, the problem is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete even when the description of the agent is known. Finally, safety is not a compositional property, i.e., agents that can be proven safe on their own can still produce unsafe behavior when grouped together. We also discuss relaxed notions of safety that could be used in practice.

Toxic language detection for large language model safety has largely been framed as binary classification, yet unethical expressions differ in severity across types and human judgments of severity are far from uniform. We analyze a large-scale Korean ethics-verification corpus with eight type labels (seven unethical types plus neutral) and the individual intensity votes (0–3) of five raters per sentence (363,154 sentences; 1,001,030 votes). First, the seven unethical types form a three-tier perceived-severity hierarchy—censure (1.42) < discrimination, hate, and abuse (1.53–1.59) < sexual, violence and crime incitement (1.74–1.75)—supported by post-hoc tests: all between-tier differences are significant with substantial effect sizes (Holm-corrected p < 0.05; |Cliff’s δ| = 0.14–0.45), while within-tier effects are negligible. Second, automatically estimated sentiment valence barely explains the hierarchy (Spearman ρ = −0.142; AUC = 0.621; replicated with a Korean-specific sentiment model and with preceding dialogue context included in the input); the two most severe types show the most neutral surface valence, so sentiment signals capture best precisely the least severe type. Third, inter-rater agreement is low (ordinal Krippendorff’s α = 0.373), yet the disagreement is not explained by the basic demographics the corpus records—rater gender and age (equivalence tests bound the pooled gender effect at |d|≤0.013 and the age correlation at |ρ|≤0.002; unrecorded rater characteristics remain untested)—and instead grows with item severity (sentence-level ρ = 0.248). Harmfulness judgment appears to be a dimension largely independent of sentiment, whose annotation may benefit from continuous scales, multi-rater averaging, and severity-proportional rating resources.

documents.abstract: First-principles structural relaxation and band calculations require substantial computation and expertise. Here we present Perfumer, a large language model-based agentic framework that couples Quantum ESPRESSO with two predictive models. Across tested structures, pre-relaxation with Perfumer-relax model followed by QE refinement yielded a 2.75-fold overall speedup over QE alone. Perfumer-band model combines a periodic graph neural network with a latent Hermitian spectral head returns 12 band energies at any requested wavevector, preserving reciprocal lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry without constructing Hamiltonian. Trained on 125,153 self-curated band structures, Perfumer-band model reaches a median per-material mean absolute error of 0.157 eV on 2,607 test materials, including lanthanide, actinide and magnetic compounds, from held-out composition families spanning 85 elements, taking about 97 ms per material on two consumer CPU cores. The agent turns natural-language requests into relaxation-to-band workflows, from a single uploaded structure to automatically constructed new candidates and returns predicted properties.

documents.abstract: Public trust is central to the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital medicine, yet little is known about how patients respond to different forms of physician AI disclosure across clinical risk contexts. In a 5 × 2 factorial experiment in mainland China, 1574 adults were randomly assigned to physician profiles varying by AI use type and condition severity. Administrative AI was rated more favorably than diagnostic and therapeutic AI across physician perception and care-seeking intention outcomes. High-severity conditions amplified negative responses to therapeutic AI, whereas explicit non-AI disclosure was associated with greater appointment willingness under high severity. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that competence, trust, and empathy accounted for different disclosure-related response patterns. Main effects were directionally consistent in a supplementary offline community sample from Macao ( n = 128). These findings suggest that AI disclosure in digital medicine should distinguish administrative from clinical uses and be calibrated to clinical severity, while highlighting the need for preregistered replication using behavioral outcomes.

documents.abstract: Developing generalizable, data-efficient machine learning (ML) models for advanced manufacturing remains challenging because experimental datasets are limited and process-property relationships vary across materials and operating conditions. In laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), melt pool width, depth, and melting mode (conduction, transition, or keyhole) govern process stability and defect formation. Conventional ML models typically use dimensional process parameters, which represent laser-material interactions only implicitly and may limit cross-material transfer. This study evaluates whether two physics-informed dimensionless features, normalized enthalpy and Peclet number, combining laser processing conditions with material thermophysical properties, improve melt pool prediction over raw process parameters. We systematically benchmark seven models: four classical ML methods (Gaussian process, support vector machine, random forest, and XGBoost) and three pretrained tabular foundation models (TabPFN, TabDPT, and TabICLv2). Experiments span 316L stainless steel, IN625, IN718, and combined-material datasets, covering regression of melt pool width and depth and classification of melting modes. Dimensionless features yield comparable or superior predictive performance in most settings, with the largest gains in cross-material depth prediction (R^2 = 0.96). Tabular foundation models generally achieve stronger classification performance than classical baselines, particularly for multi-material datasets. These findings indicate that combining physically meaningful dimensionless representations with pretrained tabular models can improve data-efficient melt pool modeling and support more transferable process-window identification in LPBF.

Recent work reports strong pragmatic performance by large language models (LLMs) in English, yet whether this performance generalises across languages and evaluation settings remains unclear. This question is increasingly important as LLMs are deployed across languages, cultures, and conversational contexts. In this paper, we first introduce PILAPS, a bilingual English/Mandarin Chinese benchmark covering eight pragmatic phenomena across purpose-written and dialogue-derived items, with both culturally adapted and independently sourced data. We then evaluate eight LLMs from four families across a range of model sizes and prompting strategies. Our results reveal substantial variation across models and pragmatic phenomena: open-source models continue to struggle particularly with humour, while cross-linguistic performance varies with model origin. Our error analysis shows that, compared with human participants, models are more prone to literal interpretations in conversational contexts. Theory-of-Mind prompting lowers the literal share of errors, whereas Chain-of-Thought prompting slightly raises it. Together, these findings demonstrate that strong pragmatic performance in one evaluation setting does not necessarily generalise across languages or conversational contexts.

Effective task and project management needs efficient task prioritization, scheduling, progress monitoring, and coordination among people, all things considered. Conventional task management systems mostly rest on manual planning and tracking, which can make it difficult for users to manage competing priorities and changing workloads. This paper introduces PlanWise, an AI-powered personal and collaborative task management system designed to support task organization, project coordination, and intelligent productivity assistance, at least in principle. A web-based interface with backend services and database management is being blended by this setup to support personal tasks and collaborative project workflows, and includes large language model-based AI assistance for daily planning, task guidance, and project intelligence, combining task-related information and deterministic processing with AI-generated explanations and recommendations. It also is stressing user control by requiring approval for AI-suggested changes before they're employed. PlanWise is built using React and Vite for the frontend and Supabase for authentication, database operations, and backend functionality, with Google Gemini API integration for AI-assisted attributes. This paper is outlining the system architecture, design methodology, implementation approach, and evaluation framework. In fact, the current implementation founds for integrating AI assistance into the personal and collaborative task management. Further testing is required for the assessment of the reliability, potency and concrete benefits of its AI-driven capabilities. Keywords—Artificial Intelligence, Task Management, Project Management, Large Language Models, Intelligent Planning, Human-AI Interaction

documents.abstract: Generative AI is changing not only how content is created on digital content platforms but also who provides the AI used to create it. Platforms may offer generative AI using data pooled across creators, whereas creators may provide AI services based on their own content. Understanding how these provision regimes affect creators’ investment incentives and the value generated by AI is therefore important. We develop a game-theoretic model in which human-generated content competes with AI-generated content while contributing to AI learning. The results show that platform provision can induce higher human-generated content quality than creator provision when AI learning effectiveness lies within a certain range and the platform’s pooled-data advantage is limited. A stronger pooled-data advantage can make creator provision more favorable for sustaining human-generated content quality. Platform provision can nevertheless generate higher AI-generated content quality even when creator provision induces higher human-generated content quality, provided that the pooled-data advantage is sufficiently strong. We further find that AI value sharing can encourage or discourage quality investment under platform provision, while its effects on regime preferences and preference alignment depend on market conditions. Thus, the provision regime preferred by the creator need not be the one that sustains higher human-generated content quality.

Recent AI agents can generate playable games, but these games are not necessarily engaging. Mastery is a key source of engagement, yet designing for it requires extensive human play and tuning. We propose PlayCraft, an automated framework that uses a vision-based agent to play games and draws on its detailed play experience to revise them for mastery. Starting from an initial game, PlayCraft alternates between playing and crafting. In the playing stage, a player agent watches the game screen, uses the controls, and pursues the game objective over repeated episodes while retaining memory. After each episode, it reports its progress, outcomes, decisions, and reflections. In the crafting stage, a crafter agent uses these reports to revise the game. It estimates player abilities, predicts performance at different proficiency levels, and compares those predictions with a target learning progression. It diagnoses the game and addresses the gaps by giving players meaningful opportunities to improve through better decisions and execution. We evaluate games in fresh runs with player agents across three intelligence settings, measuring learning gain and learning slope. Compared with the initial games, PlayCraft yields larger learning gains and steeper learning slopes in most games. It also outperforms the baselines on the macro-average of each metric at every intelligence setting.

documents.abstract: OBJECTIVES First responders often work in unpredictable, uncontrolled environments, where exposure to infected patients and contaminated environments heighten the risk of communicable disease transmission. Their higher infection prevalence compared with the general population has driven the implementation of personal protective equipment, vaccination requirements, safety protocols, and infection prevention education. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to estimate the pooled prevalence of infections among first responders in the prehospital workers including paramedics, emergency medical technicians, patient transport staff, firefighters, police, and police officers.METHODS Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science and PUBMED/Medline were systematically searched. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation, with Freeman–Tukey double-arcsine transformation and back-transformation to the original prevalence scale. Heterogeneity was assessed using I², τ², and 95% prediction intervals. Meta-regression was used to examine potential sources of between-study heterogeneity, and small-study effects and potential publication bias were assessed using funnel plots and Egger’s regression test. Risk of bias was investigated using the AXIS tool.RESULTS Following the initial search, 34,874 articles were identified, of which 88 were full-text screened. Of these, 22 studies representing 19,188 first responders were included in this systematic review. The pooled prevalences of hepatitis B and C were 6.2% (95% CI 4.5%-8.2%) and 1.8% (95% CI 0.9%-2.9%), respectively. Around 4% (95% CI 2.6%- 5.9%) of the first responders had MRSA colonisation. Current or past infection with COVID-19 among non-vaccinated first responders was 13.6% (95% CI 4.8%- 25.9%), which reduced to 7.3% (95% CI 3.6%- 12%) after exclusion of studies with high risk of bias. Of the known study characteristics, geographic region significantly contributed to heterogeneity, explaining 36.7% of between-study variance, p = 0.039.CONCLUSIONS Infectious disease prevalence varied across pathogens, occupations, and geographical settings among first responders. These findings should be interpreted in light of substantial heterogeneity and limitations in the available evidence but may help inform infection prevention, occupational health policy, vaccination strategies, and future research in first responder services.

documents.abstract: The increasing global population has intensified the demand for food, placing significant pressure on agricultural systems to enhance productivity while ensuring environmental sustainability. This review examines the integration of the Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) in digital crop management, drawing on the technologies and applications discussed in the manuscript. Precision agriculture has emerged as an effective approach for optimising resource use by managing spatial and temporal variability within fields. It integrates advanced technologies such as the Global Positioning System, Geographic Information Systems, variable-rate technology, auto-steer guidance systems, wireless telematics, remote sensing, artificial intelligence and yield monitoring systems to support site-specific crop management. The adoption of the Internet of Things has further strengthened precision agriculture by enabling real-time monitoring of soil, crop and environmental parameters through sensor networks. These sensors generate continuous field data that facilitate informed decision-making and efficient resource utilisation. Furthermore, the large volume of data produced by IoT-based systems can be effectively analysed using machine learning techniques. As a subset of AI, ML enables the identification of patterns and generation of predictive insights for applications such as crop yield prediction, irrigation scheduling, nutrient management and weed detection, thereby enhancing productivity and sustainability in modern agriculture.

HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod) steels are promising candidates for advanced nuclear fuel cladding. In this study, 1,590 tensile test data points of 9–12Cr ferritic/martensitic (FM) steels were collected to develop machine learning (ML) models for predicting irradiation-induced changes in the tensile properties of HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod). Regression models were evaluated after Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization using test-set evaluation and k -fold cross-validation (CV). Extreme gradient boosting (XGB) exhibited the best predictive performance; however, an artificial neural network (ANN) was selected for its continuous response, physical consistency, and stable representation of irradiation-dependent trends. Using independent experimental data, the ANN yielded mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) of 6.26 ± 0.47% for ultimate tensile strength (UTS) and 10.69 ± 0.46% for yield strength (YS). The ANN model predicted the YS across irradiation conditions and showed that the irradiation-induced increase in YS for HT9 and Gr.92 (Mod) steels saturated at 5–10 displacements per atom (dpa). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) method, quantified the contributions of dpa and irradiation temperature, revealing that irradiation temperature has a greater overall influence on the predicted YS. These results provide both reliable property predictions and physical insights into the effects of irradiation conditions.

Multi-panel figures are commonly used in research papers to show scientific data, and researchers often reuse them when presenting their work. Presenting these figures often involves explaining how data across chart panels are related. Animated transitions can progressively reveal these relationships, but two static panels specify only the endpoints, leaving what intermediate keyframes should show and how the transition should progress unclear. To support transition design across diverse scientific figures, we developed Figure Space and Transition Space through iterative analysis of 48 published multi-panel figures across eight scientific subject areas. Figure Space represents panel composition, data transformations, and visual encodings while retaining the links needed to trace panel results back to records. Transition Space uses this representation and source data to construct and sequence keyframes that make corresponding data visible and align them while preserving the meaning of each panel's position encodings. Building on these spaces, we developed FigFlux, a human-in-the-loop authoring system that guides AI agents in generating animated transitions from a multi-panel figure and its associated materials. Researchers can revise keyframes in natural language before animation generation. We evaluate FigFlux through cross-domain case studies, a study with 16 scientific authors, and expert assessment. Authors reported lower overall workload than with their familiar tools, while experts gave FigFlux transitions higher ratings than transitions created with participants' familiar tools or generated by AI alone. The example gallery have been published online: https://figflux.github.io.

Aims: To assess the prevalence of musculoskeletal disorders among shrimp farm workers and examine their association with selected demographic characteristics. Study Design: A descriptive research design was adopted for the study. Place and Duration of Study: The study was conducted between 2023–2026 in the selected shrimp farming areas of Andhra Pradesh (Kakinada, West Godavari and Bapatla districts) and Telangana (Narayanpet, Jogulamba Gadwal and Wanaparthy districts). Methodology: A total of 150 shrimp farm workers were selected through purposive sampling based on their involvement in shrimp-farming activities. Data were collected using a researcher-developed structured interview schedule covering demographic and occupational characteristics and self-reported musculoskeletal disorders across different body regions. Frequencies, percentages, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and correlation analysis were used for statistical analysis. Results: Among the participants, 93.33 per cent were male and 68.67 per cent were engaged in elementary occupations. Upper back pain was frequently reported by 47.33 per cent of workers on the right side and 20 per cent on the left side. The corresponding percentages for lower back pain were 46 and 24 per cent, respectively, while wrist pain was reported by 44 per cent on the right side and 41.33 per cent on the left side. Muscle cramps were reported as occurring sometimes by 59.33 per cent on the right side and 55.33 per cent on the left side. Right-sided symptom scores were higher than left-sided scores, with a statistically significant difference between the two sides (Wilcoxon signed-rank test: Z = −8.686, p < 0.001). A statistically significant difference was observed in overall musculoskeletal discomfort scores across the occupational groups (Kruskal–Wallis H = 7.163, df = 2, p = 0.028). Pearson’s correlation analysis showed no statistically significant relationships between overall MSD scores and age, education, socioeconomic status or monthly income (p > 0.05). Conclusion: The study highlighted the occurrence of musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) among shrimp farm workers and the need for attention to their occupational health. The findings provided a basis for identifying work-related ergonomic problems and developing suitable interventions, worker awareness programmes and regular health assessments to improve occupational health and safety in shrimp farming.

documents.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can now autonomously conduct AI research by writing code and running experiments. They typically do so by iteratively optimizing a codebase, while ignoring the problem structure behind the task. This formulation is effective on simpler tasks, but on difficult problems it often gets stuck in the wrong solution region because the agent never explicitly represents its understanding of the problem. We introduce Pro$^2$ Agent, which shifts the primary state of autonomous AI research from a codebase state to a Problem State: an explicit structure of what problems prevent success and which solutions are likely to address them. Pro$^2$ Agent initializes the Problem State through comprehensive analysis of available resources and constraints. It then performs targeted research to relate the identified problems to candidate solutions. Through controlled hypothesis testing, the agent updates the importance of a suspected problem or the benefit brought by a candidate solution. On the complete MLE-Bench, Pro$^2$ Agent matches the best reported medal rate (70.7%) under the standard 24-hour budget and reaches 76.0% with a 48-hour budget, the highest medal rate reported on the complete benchmark. It also achieves competitive performance on PostTrainBench. In addition, it produces research notes for each task that make the research process transparent and reusable by human researchers.

This paper explores the role of Large Language Models (LLMs) in promoting sustainable behavior, specifically in overcoming procrastination. Despite widespread recognition of the need for sustainable behavior change, individuals often struggle to break free from entrenched, unsustainable habits. LLMs, such as OpenAI’s GPT-4, represent a significant breakthrough in artificial intelligence and are increasingly used in behavior change interventions. This study introduces ProactiMate, a chatbot built using Motivational Interviewing (MI) principles and a Chain of Models approach for prompt engineering, designed to help users combat procrastination. Our research compares four LLMs (GPT-3.5 Turbo, LLaMA-3.2, Qwen-2.5, and SmolLM-1.7B) for output influence on procrastination avoidance, and assesses the impact of hyperparameters (temperature and top-p values) on procrastination avoidance. The findings reveal that GPT-3.5 outperforms other models across various evaluation metrics, and higher temperature and top-p values lead to more effective procrastination avoidance from automatic evaluation. According to expert evaluations, Qwen-2.5 and GPT-3.5 Turbo demonstrated notable effectiveness in fostering user engagement and motivation for addressing procrastination, with GPT-3.5 Turbo particularly distinguished by its capacity to provide strategies that help maintain long-term motivation. And GPT’s output aligns well with both automatic evaluation metrics and human evaluation. The results provide insights into the most effective ways to use LLMs in chatbot design, offering solutions for future usability testing.

This study aimed to determine the psychometric properties of the School Task Engagement Scale (ECTE) among primary school students from UGEL Santa, 2026. A basic, quantitative, non-experimental, cross-sectional study with a descriptive-instrumental scope was conducted. The sample consisted of 300 fourth-, fifth-, and sixth-grade students selected through proportional stratified probability sampling. Data were collected through a survey using the 18-item ECTE, which measures affective, behavioral, and cognitive engagement. Content validity was assessed by five experts, yielding an overall Aiken’s V of 1.00 for clarity, relevance, and coherence. The three-factor model showed acceptable fit indices (χ²/df = 2.18; RMSEA = 0.063; SRMR = 0.044; CFI = 0.921; TLI = 0.909), and factor loadings were above 0.50. Cronbach’s alpha values for the dimensions ranged from 0.765 to 0.787, while McDonald’s omega ranged from 0.766 to 0.792. The overall scale yielded α = 0.914 and ω = 0.916. The findings provide favorable evidence of validity and reliability in the studied sample, although generalization to other populations requires further research.

documents.abstract: Protokół zadania 0.4 programu badawczego monografii „Świadomość sytuacyjna na rynku mieszkaniowym. Rama pojęciowa, narzędzie pomiaru i program badawczy“, wraz z aneksami nr 1 i nr 2, wynikiem rozpoznania zbiorów oraz audytem katalogów zmiennych programu HFCS. Zadanie przewidywało częściowy i zastępczy test dwóch hipotez rdzeniowych — H-C o miskalibracji kompetencji oraz H-E o spójności międzypoziomowej — na danych panelowych pochodzących ze zbiorów istniejących. Protokół określa zmienne wymagane, zbiory do sprawdzenia i regułę rozstrzygania przed przystąpieniem do rozpoznania. Rozpoznanie zamknięto wynikiem negatywnym w zakresie krajowym. Żaden ze sprawdzonych zbiorów obejmujących Polskę nie zawiera pomiaru horyzontu planowania gospodarstwa domowego, będącego pierwszym składnikiem wskaźnika różnicowego wymaganego przez H-E, ani obiektywnego pomiaru kompetencji finansowej, co wyklucza również H-C. Aneks nr 1 zamknął rozpoznanie na podstawie katalogu zmiennych fali 2017; aneks nr 2 sprostował jego uzasadnienie po audycie katalogów fal 2021 i 2023, nie zmieniając kierunku rozstrzygnięcia. Audyt wykazał, że oba składniki wskaźnika wymaganego przez H-E nie były dostępne jednocześnie w żadnej z pięciu fal programu HFCS. Depozyt ma charakter dokumentacyjny: nastąpił po zamknięciu rozpoznania i nie pełni funkcji preregistracyjnej. Udostępnia procedurę, bez której wynik negatywny pozostawałby nieweryfikowalny — czytelnik nie mógłby sprawdzić, czy zbiorów szukano właściwie. Na tej samej procedurze opierają się dwa opracowania wykazane w aneksie preregistracyjnym monografii: inwentarz par zmiennych o pojemności różnicowej oraz procedura datowania statusu zmiennych w kolejnych falach badania. ——— English summary. Protocol for task 0.4 of the research programme accompanying the monograph „Situational awareness in the housing market“ (in Polish), with two annexes, the outcome of the dataset review and an audit of HFCS variable catalogues. The task was designed as a partial, surrogate test of two core hypotheses on existing household panel data. The review closed with a null result for Poland: none of the datasets examined measures the household planning horizon, nor does any contain an objective measure of financial competence. The audit shows that the two components of the differential indicator required by hypothesis H-E were never simultaneously available in any of the five HFCS waves. This deposit is documentary, not a pre-registration: it was made after the review had closed and makes no claim of priority. It publishes the procedure, without which the null result could not be verified.

Virtual environments are often added to exercise equipment to make exercise more engaging, although previous work has often emphasised enjoyment. This exploratory within-subject study compared stationary cycling with screen-based virtual cycling in 15 adults (6 women, 9 men; aged 20–59 years). Each participant completed one 10-min, self-paced session in each condition, in counterbalanced order, on the same recumbent bicycle with fixed resistance. After each session, participants completed the Intrinsic Motivation Inventory and rated their perceived exertion (Borg 6–20); heart rate and cadence were recorded every minute. Enjoyment was higher after virtual cycling (mean difference 2.31 points on a 1–7 scale, 95% CI [1.61, 3.00]), as was value/usefulness (1.38 [0.56, 2.20]); 14 and 12 participants, respectively, reported higher scores. Both paired t-test differences remained after Holm correction. Differences in perceived competence, effort/importance, and pressure/tension were smaller, with confidence intervals including zero. Heart rate (4.9 bpm, 95% CI [-0.04, 9.8]) and cadence (2.8 rpm [-2.4, 7.9]) showed no clear difference between conditions. Perceived exertion was slightly higher during virtual cycling (0.8 points [0.01, 1.59]), but this difference did not remain after correction. Power output was not measured, so workload could not be compared directly. Enjoyment was strongly correlated with value/usefulness during virtual cycling (r = 0.87, 95% CI [0.64, 0.95]); individual responses also varied, particularly in perceived competence. Given the small sample and single 10-min session per condition, larger studies should measure workload directly and examine responses across repeated sessions.

Video Large Language Models process large numbers of visual tokens, making token pruning important for efficient inference. Training-free pruning methods differ in whether and how they use the user query, and the value of query conditioning remains unclear. We present a controlled study of training-free, pre-LLM video token selection. Using a shared Qwen-3-VL backbone, token budgets, and decoding settings, we compare 21 pruning principles spanning query-agnostic, shallow query-conditioned, structured query-conditioned, and holistic strategies. To instantiate the last two categories, we introduce Structured Query Pruning, which decomposes the question into semantic anchors, and a Pareto variant, which combines anchor relevance with query-agnostic visual diversity. Across Video-MME, MVBench, and LongVideoBench, relevance computed from the raw question embedding is unreliable (8--16 points below the best methods), whereas anchors derived from query decomposition avoid this failure. However, query access is not inherently advantageous: strong query-agnostic coverage methods remain competitive or superior in the full-field comparison. Relative to a redundancy-only baseline, structured selection helps most on evidence-specific and long-context tasks at tight budgets; on broad tasks, the holistic selector improves over either relevance or redundancy alone. Further, pruning reduces cost and memory. These results support a practical design rule: preserve visual coverage by default, and add structured relevance when the task and token budget demand selective evidence retrieval.

Background Systematic review software must coordinate independent human decisions, protocol amendments and heterogeneous information sources. Synchronizing reviewers at every stage can create waiting time unrelated to the scientific assessment of a record. We describe R-SYS, a workflow that links decisions to versioned protocols and allows reviewers to progress independently before a final reconciliation step. Methods The reference implementation combines an eleven-phase guarded lifecycle, immutable locked protocol versions, deterministic rendering of a canonical search strategy, per-reviewer working sets and decision provenance. Each primary reviewer advances through title and abstract screening, full-text assessment, extraction and risk-of-bias appraisal using their own preceding decisions, subject to human adjudication. A final convergence checkpoint resolves outstanding work before synthesis. Artificial intelligence (AI) supplies advisory recommendations that are excluded from human reconciliation. We analyse completion times under explicit scheduling assumptions and describe implementation limitations. Results With identical task sets, continuous reviewer availability and no external waiting, independent lanes achieve a completion time equal to the largest reviewer workload. This is a lower bound for schedules that impose additional synchronization constraints. Disagreement can introduce superseded work and delays; a sufficient condition for retaining an advantage over stage barriers is stated. The implementation provides mechanisms for protocol change control, reviewer coordination and traceable reporting. No empirical measurements of accuracy, efficiency, usability or cost are reported. Conclusions R-SYS provides a reference design for separating reviewer independence from workflow synchronization. Its theoretical scheduling properties do not establish practical time savings, search completeness or AI accuracy. A separate, prospectively specified validation study is planned after completed reviews using the platform become available.

Diagnostic radiologists spend much of their professional time interpreting imaging studies using a variety of workstation and monitor configurations. Despite well-established ergonomic principles, there are no widely accepted recommendations regarding monitor configuration, application placement, or peripheral device selection. This variability, particularly across academic medical centers with diverse workstation configurations, may contribute to musculoskeletal injury, workflow inefficiency, cognitive burden, and challenges integrating artificial intelligence (AI) applications. This study characterizes radiologist workstation configurations and determines whether similar usage patterns emerge across two independent national needs assessments. The findings from both assessments were compared. The first consisted of live audience polling during an RSNA 2025 educational session on radiologist ergonomics (n = 54). The second was an online survey distributed through professional LinkedIn and radiology social media communities (n = 49). Survey questions evaluated monitor number and orientation, workstation layout, application placement, ergonomic practices, sit-stand workstation use, and peripheral devices. Both assessments demonstrated similar workstation preferences. Most respondents in both the RSNA poll (n = 54) and online needs assessment (n = 49) used four-monitor equivalent configurations consisting of two portrait diagnostic monitors (often combined into one 30″ landscape) flanked by two supplemental monitors. Dictation was most commonly displayed on the left supplemental monitor, adjacent to the current examination (on the left diagnostic monitor). Respondents reported diverse placement of worklists, thumbnails, AI tools, peer review, electronic medical records, and advanced visualization applications. Sit-stand workstations were widely used, with most respondents standing 10-30% of the workday. Gaming mice with hyperscrolling functionality were the predominant pointing devices with very similar functions (window/level, measure, arrow, zoom/pan, and ROI). Two independent national needs assessments revealed consistent patterns in radiologist workstation configurations despite differences in survey methodology and participant populations. These findings suggest an emerging, flexible de facto standard that could guide ergonomic recommendations, workstation design and procurement, residency training, workflow optimization, and AI integration.

documents.abstract: Persistent, channel-organized communication environments give instructors ways to arrange questions, assistance, announcements, and informal interaction alongside a learning management system. Their use depends on how students enter the environment, how information and audiences are organized, who provides assistance, and how participation is experienced. This conceptual article presents Real-Time Academic Platform Integration Design (RAPID), a descriptive framework developed through a focused synthesis of 37 publications and a source-anchored matrix of 750 evidence items. Following a bounded literature search with artificial intelligence support for screening and extraction, the authors reviewed source evidence and selected and refined the framework by comparing model-generated alternatives. RAPID comprises four components: Student Onboarding, Environment Organization, Sustainable Help, and Student Participation and Social Climate, interpreted through an affordance perspective and Community of Inquiry. A constructed LMS-centered baseline, two reflective teaching illustrations, and a literature-informed projection show how it applies across differences in course size, staffing, and participation requirements. The framework’s usefulness, workload implications, and relationship to learning require empirical study.

Introduction to Business is often a student’s first encounter with how organizations plan, take risks, communicate, and answer for their decisions. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how students research and write, and how colleges increasingly recognize neurodiverse ways of learning. Together these make the first business course a natural place to reconsider what introductory business education can be. This paper describes a redesign of BUS 101 at Barton College’s School of Business & Innovation, being delivered in Fall 2026 across three sections taught by three instructors. The redesign treats the course itself as a working business environment. Syllabus policies become exercises in applied risk ethics: a “24-Hour High-Risk Window” and a one-time “Stuff Happens Pass” modeled on a contingency reserve. Academic integrity rests on process rather than detection, through visible revision histories and a Socratic oral defense. Presentations carry 40% of the grade, personal finance is taught as a form of self-governance and a gateway to business finance, and qualitative video reflections complement numerical ratings. Shared cross-section sessions with industry speakers provide continuity while preserving each instructor’s approach. Drawing on process philosophy, the ethics of responsibility, and experiential learning theory, we set out the design’s rationale, its implementation to date, and a research agenda whose results will be reported in a follow-up study.

Large language models (LLMs) have clear potential to contribute to psychological research methods. However, as with any new research method, LLM-based methods require rigorous evaluation. Towards this end, Austin and colleagues evaluated the ability of two LLMs (GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Flash) to facilitate scale validation by identifying relevant criterion measures and generating validity hypotheses for assessing convergent and discriminant validity. We argue that their study has several key limitations that limit the conclusions that can be drawn about the proposed method's suitability for use in validation research. We situate our critique within three recommendations for incorporating LLMs into research: (a) avoid essentialisation and overgeneralisation about 'AI', (b) use application programming interfaces when evaluating LLMs in research contexts and (c) evaluate LLM-based methods using clearly specified criteria. Finally, we consider whether adopting the proposed method might reinforce or amplify existing limitations in the psychological literature, namely, the proliferation of overlapping constructs and inadequately validated measures.

Clinical AI is moving from systems that generate discrete predictions and recommendations toward agents capable of pursuing clinical objectives through repeated tool use, communication, planning, and state-changing actions. Emerging systems support multistep electronic health record workflows, and increasingly envision longitudinal care across repeated encounters. This transition expands safety assessment beyond discrete outputs and actions. Through its actions, an agent can help create the clinical state on which its subsequent decisions depend. Consequently, individually defensible actions may compose into an unsafe trajectory, even when no single action is clearly erroneous. We propose recoverability-centered trajectory governance as a clinical synthesis of established safety approaches, linking patient-specific corrective capacity to the continuing justification for delegated authority. Its central objective is clinical recoverability: preserving the opportunity for the human-AI care system to redirect care before clinically acceptable corrective pathways are exhausted. We define recovery margin as the remaining opportunity for such correction, and reauthorization boundaries as conditions requiring delegated authority to end or narrow pending renewed human judgment. This framing distinguishes reversibility, primarily a property of an action, from recoverability, a property of an evolving clinical trajectory. The operational framework combines persistent obligation tracking, independent monitoring, explicit reauthorization, authority contraction, graceful degradation, independent escalation, and verified human takeover. Oversight should concentrate at consequential trajectory junctions. Evaluation should combine trajectory stress testing, component-specific recovery-margin indicators, interruption-and-takeover testing, and population-level surveillance. Trajectory governance complements product lifecycle oversight by examining whether continued patient-specific delegation remains justified as care evolves. Because corrective capacity depends partly on access to timely monitoring and human rescue, recoverability is also an equity issue. The defining safety question is therefore not only whether an action is acceptable but whether continued delegation remains justified. The proposed indicators and governance mechanisms require domain-specific operationalization and empirical validation, including comparison with established safeguards.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Australia’s growing demand for science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) skills contrasts with stagnant tertiary participation and persistent inequities. This brief review examines barriers to inclusive tertiary STEM education and the potential for artificial intelligence (AI) to support Universal Design for Learning. AI can provide multimodal content, personalised scaffolding, flexible participation and assessment, and support for self-regulated and collaborative learning. Effective adoption therefore requires institutional governance, AI proficiency and sustained educator judgement. Further longitudinal research in Australian tertiary STEM settings is needed to identify which tools reduce barriers, for whom and under what conditions.

Existing studies have primarily focused on the effects of artificial intelligence (AI) on productivity and carbon emission efficiency, while systematic evidence on whether and through which mechanisms AI improves agricultural ecological efficiency (AEE) remains relatively limited. Using provincial panel data from China for the period 2005 to 2023, this study employs the entropy weighting method to measure regional AI development and a slack-based measure (SBM) model incorporating undesirable outputs to evaluate AEE. A two-way fixed effects model is further constructed to examine the effects of AI on AEE and the underlying mechanisms. AI is conceptually distinct from general digitalization, automation, precision agriculture, and information technology development, as its defining feature lies in leveraging machine learning, intelligent sensing, and algorithmic decision-making to achieve more advanced data processing and intelligent decision-making capabilities. The results indicate that a 0.1-unit increase in regional AI development is associated with an average increase of 0.01078 units in AEE. Mechanism analysis suggests that AI can indirectly improve AEE by promoting green finance development and industrial structure upgrading. Furthermore, agricultural technological innovation exhibits a significant threshold effect, with higher levels of technological innovation strengthening the positive effect of AI on AEE. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the positive effect of AI on AEE is more pronounced in eastern regions, regions with lower levels of urbanization and agricultural modernization, and non-major grain-producing regions. Further analysis identifies positive spatial spillover effects of AI on AEE in neighboring regions, contributing to coordinated green agricultural development across local and neighboring regions. This study provides evidence on the effects, transmission mechanisms, and threshold conditions through which AI improves AEE, offering new empirical insights into the role of AI in facilitating the green transformation of agriculture and extending the analytical perspective of agricultural sustainability research.
topics: Digitalization and Economic Development in Agriculture

documents.abstract: Global medium-range weather forecasting must not only generate ensembles efficiently to characterize uncertainty in future states, but also serve downstream applications such as extreme-event warnings and cross-sphere coupled simulations. We introduce WeatherCraft, a framework that unifies probabilistic generation and reinforcement learning alignment through discrete weather tokens, bringing the GPT-style pretraining--post-training paradigm to global medium-range weather forecasting. A multiscale tokenizer represents atmospheric states as a coarse-to-fine token hierarchy, while a Transformer models causal dependencies across time and scale and predicts tokens within each scale in parallel. Direct sampling generates diverse ensembles, and exact token log-probabilities enable Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to maximize downstream task rewards without differentiating through evaluators or coupled models. On the ERA5 benchmark, WeatherCraft's eight-member ensemble mean reduces day-15 normalized RMSE by 17.6% relative to the strongest evaluated deterministic baseline and, with KV caching, achieves an approximately $18\times$ inference speedup over GenCast. Direct fair-CRPS adaptation improves ensemble probabilistic skill, while reward-based post-training improves forecasts of persistent land temperature extremes and coupled ocean heat extremes. This work establishes discrete autoregressive modeling as a general foundation for scalable, task-alignable Earth system foundation models.

Analog layout generators provide a programmable interface for design reuse and process migration, but their coverage is limited by handcrafted libraries. The designer knowledge embedded in complete layouts remains implicit in their geometry, making it difficult to capture in reusable generator libraries. We present ReLay, a bidirectional layout-code framework that recovers generator programs from existing layouts, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing of existing designs. Constructions that recur across recovered programs are promoted to library functions, so the library evolves as layouts accumulate. We also introduce the first layout-code benchmark: 1,050 hand-drawn layouts from 27 circuit families across three open-source PDKs, ranging from primitive cells to full chips. Learned functions account for 53-66% of layout-building calls in held-out layouts, demonstrating reuse beyond the learning corpus. Frontier LLM agents use ReLay to produce new layouts at 64-77% lower API cost per completed task than direct geometry generation, with comparable completion rates and electrical quality.

Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. Agents built on five current GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models made the reported mistake in 18% to 33% of runs, against at most 1% without the blamed cause. Of the 72 incidents with real-world harm, 62 had no underlying attacker, and in these, agents did what their task asked for but missed an ordinary hazard, such as a database shared with the live site. Replications without an attacker caused more harm than replications of prompt injection for all five models. Defenses against prompt injection look for injected instructions, but these replications contain none. Further, a warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence lowered harm for all five models, whereas a note of the same length that does not mention the hazard left most of the harm in place. Built from real incidents, the ROGUE-AI replications form a reusable audit framework that vendors can rerun before each new release.

This repository provides the complete Python implementation and verified experimental results associated with the research article entitled “AI-Based Bearing Fault Classification Using Vibration Sensor Data: Effects of Signal Representations and Decision Thresholds.” The study investigates the effects of dimensionless vibration features, signal representations, physical-time dynamics, and source-derived decision thresholds on artificial intelligence-based bearing fault classification. Experiments were conducted using 59 source recordings from the MCC5–THU three-phase asynchronous motor dataset and 32 target recordings from the University of Ottawa Electric Motor Dataset. Five predefined feature and temporal configurations, 11 classification models, and four decision rules were evaluated. The models include physical-time spiking neural networks, a memoryless SNN counterpart, conventional machine learning classifiers, and ensemble methods. Model training, calibration, and decision threshold selection were performed exclusively on source data using nested stratified group cross-validation with three outer folds and two inner folds. The trained models were evaluated on the Ottawa recordings without target-side parameter updates. The Ottawa analyses include exploratory comparisons at the recording level. The archive contains: The complete Python source code and software dependencies. Publication Figures 5–10 in PNG and SVG formats. Publication Tables 5–8 in CSV format. Source cross-validation results and record-level predictions. Ottawa classification scores, calibration results, and decision thresholds. Group-based bootstrap results and supporting feature statistics. Experimental protocol, raw-data checksums, software environment information, and reproducibility verification reports. Numerical results were checked against the manuscript at the reported precision. The archive also includes independent verification of metrics recalculated from serialized prediction files. The original raw vibration recordings are not redistributed. They remain accessible through the original dataset repositories. Original datasets: MCC5–THU: https://doi.org/10.17632/6s3dggj9mw.1 University of Ottawa Electric Motor Dataset: https://doi.org/10.17632/msxs4vj48g.2 This repository supports transparent evaluation, independent verification, and reproducibility of the reported experimental findings.

The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into online language teaching has gained increasing attention due to its potential to enhance instructional efficiency, provide real-time feedback, and support personalized learning in EFL contexts. However, previous research has typically focused on teachers’ perceptions, readiness or challenges in using AI separately from one another, resulting in a fragmented picture of AI adoption. The present study investigates EFL teachers’ understanding of AI, the context-specific variables affecting their readiness for deploying it, and the barriers to incorporating it in online language teaching. Using semi-structured interviews with nine EFL teachers, a qualitative case study design was used, and analysis of the data was by means of thematic methods. Drawing upon the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, the study aims to understand teachers’ adoption and integration of AI Tools. The results show that teachers tend to perceive AI as a learning assistant and efficiency-oriented tool, which represents autonomous and flexible modes of learning. However, several barriers persist, including limited conceptual understanding of AI, difficulties in selecting appropriate tools, pedagogical and ethical concerns regarding student over-reliance and academic integrity, and technical constraints. The study highlights important pedagogical implications, suggesting the need for targeted professional development, clearer instructional guidelines, and institutional support to promote effective and responsible AI integration in EFL classrooms.

The advent of generative AI has provoked an ontological crisis in language education, tempting policymakers to equate machine-generated output with human interpretive capacity. This article challenges the premise that such technologies render language learning obsolete, arguing instead that an AI-saturated landscape makes robust humanistic engagement more vital than ever. Addressing the “scholar’s dilemma,” the paper proposes a structural shift in higher education from traditional silos toward horizontal, cross-disciplinary integration. Because English functions as a global lingua franca (ELF) and exerts an algorithmic hegemony over large language models (LLMs), advanced proficiency remains indispensable for critically querying these platforms. We advocate for a pedagogical evolution from the mechanical transmission of referential information (informing) to facilitating imaginative exploration (engaging). Central to this shift is the reclamation of “literature with a small l” as the primary representational material used to cultivate students’ “textual power.” By prioritizing the interpretive struggle over cognitive offloading—a tension described here as the “Picasso Paradox”—educators can formalize a “fifth skill” (complex critical thinking in English). This framework provides the cognitive foundation for students to navigate an AI-saturated world not as passive users, but as active curators equipped with ethical discernment and epistemic agency.

Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) paired with Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has become the dominant recipe for post-training LLMs on complex reasoning tasks, but has been shown to collapse the policy into a low-diversity mode. Repeated LLM outputs are nearly identical, and pass@k accuracy converges or degrades as a result. We propose ROAM-GRPO (Routed Off-mode Approach Mining for GRPO), an augmentation to the GRPO algorithm which incentivizes exploration of distinct reasoning strategies and aims to increase output creativity during evaluation. ROAM-GRPO detects well-solved problems during training and transfers them to an "off-mode" track. The model is prompted to produce distinct solution strategies to such problems, which are verified for logical validity and distinctness by an LLM judge and subsequently self-distilled into the policy. Training Qwen3.5-2b on a 1,000-problem subset of the MATH lvl5 dataset, ROAM-GRPO implementation increases peak pass@16 by 4.7% and correct embedding cosine distance by approximately 1.5-2x on a difficult evaluation set.
